title: Which Dave?
job: Organic first, then paid. Post organically on IG, FB and TikTok to test the joke cheaply. Move to paid only if, on at least one platform, average watch time is 15s or more (50% of the video) AND shares plus saves reach 10 or more per 1,000 views, and only after the user says yes to a budget. Paid: boost the organic H1 post with TikTok Spark Ads or Meta 'Use existing post' so its real comments carry over. Run H1 vs H2 vs H4 (text-only) as a cold hook test with the body unchanged, and run H5 alone in a separate retargeting ad set.
platforms: Instagram Reels (9:16) + feed static and carousel (1080x1350)
Facebook feed + Reels (4:5 feed crop, 9:16 Reels)
Not by default: LinkedIn. It is qsme.build's channel. Only if the user confirms QSME NZ posts there for small developers: the carousel as a 1080x1350 PDF with at most 3 hashtags.
core_joke_one_sentence: You ask the community page for a builder and get 212 comments about at least six different Daves, until Dave himself turns up asking which Dave they mean.

hooks.verbal_layer: "Asked the community page for a builder." (dry, tired Kiwi deadpan)
hooks.visual_layer: Kinetic text over the full-frame generic group thread (no filmed shot, no hand). A burned-in kicker 'Asked the community page for a builder.' over a big meme-caption '197 comments.'; the count jumps 197 → 205 (0.5s) → 212 (1.05s), a red-marker circle draws round 212, then 'Still no builder.' slams in at 1.3s. Hard cut to Mel's post at 2.5s.
hooks.audio_layer: Notification pings stacking up faster and faster until they almost become a beat.
hooks.why: Every NZ owner who has done this recognises it within 2 seconds. A specific number plus 'still no builder' states the whole pain in 5 words. It works with sound off and looks like a screen recording, not an ad. Rebuilt 2026-10-03 as kinetic text, so it costs nothing to make.

hooks.verbal_layer: Two voices with no context: "Just get Dave." ... "Which Dave?"
hooks.visual_layer: Full-frame screen recording. One comment bubble, 'Which Dave?', fills the screen, then zooms out to show it is one comment buried in a huge thread. It cuts straight to Mel's post card at 2.5s, so the body explains itself.
hooks.audio_layer: A few keyboard-typing clicks, then dead silence on the zoom-out.
hooks.why: Pure curiosity, and it starts on the joke itself. Sam's line no longer says 'Which Dave', so in this variant the peak becomes a reveal of WHO asked it (Dave himself). It's a cold-test challenger to H1. The fixed body now opens on Mel's post, so viewers learn it's a builder hunt by 3.5s.

hooks.verbal_layer: "I'm embarrassed to say how long I've spent reading about Daves."
hooks.visual_layer: A homeowner in bed on the selfie camera, face lit only by the phone, the thread reflected in their glasses. They're tired but amused.
hooks.audio_layer: The quiet hum of a room at night, then one ping.
hooks.why: Very relatable and personal, but it needs a real person on camera. An AI face here would edge toward a fake 'my experience' testimonial. Parked until the founder or a real owner can film it. Not in this test.

hooks.text_layer: If you've ever asked the local group for a builder...
hooks.visual_layer: Full-frame screen recording of the thread scrolling slowly under the text. No person and no hands. The text sits in the upper safe box (y 300-700).
hooks.audio_layer: A single ping, a beat of silence, then the VO.
hooks.why: Clear targeting, and 'Several of him' is the best throwaway line in the set. Rebuilt without a person, it costs nothing extra to make and becomes the third cold-test variant. It describes the pain rather than showing it, so it's expected to lose to H1, and the test exists to check that assumption.

hooks.mechanism: Visual promise (show the end first, then rewind)
hooks.verbal_layer: "Spoiler: it's this Dave. The group took 212 comments to not find him."
hooks.visual_layer: (Optional later; the only variant that needs an owner recording.) Opens on a real QSME screen (owner-recorded, hidden demo org): Dave K.'s bid opened from the Compare bids table, his name on his own priced lines. No badge or verification indicator (licence verification isn't confirmed live). Then a fast scrub backwards into the comment chaos.
hooks.audio_layer: Tape-rewind whoosh into stacked notification pings.
hooks.why: Shows the product in second 1. That suits retargeting people who already know the brand, so it runs alone in a retargeting ad set and is never compared against cold hooks. Repeating the profile shot at 21s is a deliberate bookend for this audience. It gives away the punchline, so it's paid only and never organic.

chosen_reason: H1 (mid-action start) passes the 2-second 'that's literally me' test best. In the first 3 seconds it stacks four layers: the number on screen, a deadpan spoken line, a real thumb scrolling and ping spam. It works with sound off, looks native to the feed, and sets up the Dave escalation instead of spending it. Since the 2026-10-03 rebuild it's also free to make: the whole reel is rendered from HTML with the motion kit, with no filming, no actors and no AI video. For paid, H1, H2 and H4 (text-only) run in a cold ad set with equal budgets. H5 runs alone in retargeting.

music.direction: The first half has almost no music: the notification pings ARE the soundtrack, building into an accidental rhythm. A hard 2-second silence lands on 'Dave here. Which Dave do you mean?' (the laugh), and one lonely ping lands on 'Dave can.' The music bed enters exactly at the swipe to QSME (13.5s) as the release, and resolves under the single 'ding' and the end card.
music.mood: Dry, cheeky, then relieved. Understated Kiwi, not hype. For example: clean electric or acoustic guitar, soft kit, light bass, no vocals.
music.bpm: 90-100 BPM for the groove section (13.5s to the end, ~16.5s). The ping section has no fixed tempo and just speeds up.
music.source: ONE commercially licensed music bed, mixed into the CapCut master for EVERY version (organic and paid), so all versions sound identical and the music can enter exactly at 13.5s. Use either (a) an ElevenLabs Music track on a plan that permits commercial use, prompt: 'laid-back warm guitar groove, soft drums, light bass, 95 BPM, no vocals, dry and slightly cheeky, 17 seconds, gentle entry, clean resolve at the end', or (b) a business-tier Epidemic Sound or Artlist licence (their personal and creator tiers exclude brand advertising). Do NOT add in-app music when posting: the TikTok Commercial Music Library and Meta Sound Collection play from 0s and can't be offset to the cut. SFX from ElevenLabs: 'generic soft phone notification ping, short, not iOS tri-tone, not Messenger, 5 slight pitch variations', plus a soft counter tick, one bright resolving ding, a soft swipe whoosh and a short marker squeak.
music.licensing_note: Trending copyrighted songs are licensed for personal or creator use, not brand advertising. On a business account they can get muted or taken down, and they can't go into paid ads. Before posting anything, confirm the user's ElevenLabs plan permits commercial use of the VO, SFX and music. Keep every prompt and licence receipt in projects/<slug>/outputs/licences/. No CapCut library audio in any branded export.

voice.character: Mel, the owner who posted the question. Late 30s, renovating her first place, organised, slightly worn down by the thread but amused by it. She is the straight man and never part of the mess; the thread is the joke.
voice.accent_and_delivery: General everyday New Zealand accent, the way a normal Kiwi talks to a mate. Not Australian, not posh British, not a caricature: no 'sweet as bro', no exaggerated vowels, no rising inflection on every line. Dry deadpan, under-played. The roll call 'Deck Dave. Roof Dave. Big Dave. Little Dave.' is completely flat, with a tiny pause between pairs so it lands on the scroll stops. The product lines sound like the same person, still conversational, never an announcer, and she never reads out a URL.
voice.elevenlabs_direction: First try Voice Library filtered to a New Zealand accent and shortlist 3. Test every candidate on two script lines that expose Kiwi vowels and t-tapping: 'Deck Dave. Roof Dave. Big Dave. Little Dave.' and 'Put the job on QSME. Free to join.' Reject any voice where 'deck' or 'little' sounds Aussie, or that drifts British. If none fit, use Voice Design with: 'New Zealand woman, late 30s, general everyday Kiwi accent, relaxed and dry, slightly tired deadpan humour, talks like she's telling a mate about her week, recorded close on a phone in a quiet lounge. Not Australian, not British, not American, not a newsreader, not exaggerated.' Model: Multilingual v2 by default (no audio tags are needed now). Use Eleven v3 only if the roll-call pauses need finer control. Starting settings: stability ~0.45, similarity ~0.75, style 0-0.1, speaker boost on, speed ~0.95. Generate 3 takes per line and pick in the edit. Add a pronunciation alias for QSME once the user confirms how it's said. If a URL is ever spoken in a future cut, script it as 'dot co dot en zed'. Save the chosen voice ID in ventures/qsme-nz.md. If an ElevenLabs voice ships, switch on the platform AI labels (see integrity notes).
voice.real_person_alternative: Better for trust, free, and it needs no AI label: the founder or a real Kiwi homeowner records the ~40-word VO as a phone voice memo (a wardrobe full of clothes makes a decent booth). Optional alternate end tag: a real builder who is actually on QSME, ideally really called Dave, says 'Dave here. The one who quoted.' to camera on his phone. Only with his written consent, and never 'the verified one' (licence verification isn't confirmed live). The hands in the hook shot are real hands (anyone's), so there's no AI person anywhere in the video.

production_workflow.step: 1. Pitch and get a yes (before any spend)
production_workflow.what: Show the user the 5 hooks and this package. Get answers to the blocking open questions: the exact fee line and organic-only vs a paid budget. (Since the 2026-10-02 rebuild no owner recording or demo org is needed for the main cut; only the optional H5 variant needs one.) (Pronunciation is confirmed: 'Cue Ess Me'. No licence claim is made, so 'which licences' no longer blocks.)
production_workflow.output: Approved hook (H1) and concept. Idea card status changes to 'agreed', with a dated line added to its discussion history.

production_workflow.what: Finalise the thread lines, on-screen text, timed VO script (~40 words; read it aloud against the beat sheet and it must fit inside 28s including the silences), caption, hashtags, CTA and paid ad-copy fields. Run the humor checks: one-sentence joke, works with sound off, nobody punched. Search 'Hillcrest Locals (Unofficial)' to make sure no real group uses it and record the check.

production_workflow.step: 3. Build the generic group UI kit
production_workflow.what: Auto-layout components: GroupPost, PinnedPostHeader, Comment (variants: normal / OP / Dave), a red-marker 'Dave count' tag (variants 1, 3, 6 (ish), ?, 1 with tick), a red-marker underline and circle, and initials avatars, all in a neutral palette that does not look like Facebook. Thread text at least 44px in 1080x1920 frames and at least 34px in 1080x1350 frames. Add a safe-zone overlay frame (x 65-1015, y 300-1250) to every 9:16 frame, plus a QSME end card using the real brand assets (Manrope 800, Inter, logo, colours).
production_workflow.output: Figma file 'QSME NZ - Which Dave' with components and frames

Slide 6 uses the real iPhone app still 04-project (demo data) cropped to the tile grid with the address header covered (see Figma fixes pending); no Compare bids screenshot needed. production_workflow.step: 5. Thread prototype and full-frame recording (DONE differently 2026-10-02: the whole reel is rendered from motion/which-dave-30s.html with the motion kit)

The counter uses three states (197, 205, 212) with a 0.15s Smart Animate between them, and the pings cover the jumps. Open the prototype on the phone for the hook shot. The owner screen-records QSME signed in, on a hidden demo org that is excluded from public search and the live projects map: create a project (QSME wordmark visible in the header), the tender going out, the Compare bids table (flip Excl./Incl. GST), and Dave K.'s bid opened to its own lines. No verification badge. Delete the demo data after filming. No Higgsfield, Runway or Veo.

production_workflow.tool: ElevenLabs (or a founder voice memo for the VO)
production_workflow.what: VO for Mel (3 takes per line), or the founder's phone memo. SFX: 5 generic ping variations (the prompt excludes the iOS tri-tone and the Messenger pop), a counter tick, one bright ding, a swipe and a marker squeak. One ~17s music bed used in every version. This is the only paid step: confirm the spend and that the plan permits commercial use first.

production_workflow.step: 8. Edit (picture locked 2026-10-02: outputs/which-dave-30s-9x16.mp4 and -4x5.mp4; only audio is left)
production_workflow.what: Lay the VO, SFX and music onto the locked MP4s on the 30s beat sheet: the ping rhythm, the 2s silence on Dave, the lonely ping on 'Dave can.', music in at 13.5s, and the single ding at about 22.95s. Only burn in captions for VO lines not already on screen (the hook line); the comments and on-screen text are the captions everywhere else. Check every frame against Meta's and TikTok's safe-zone overlays. Use only our own assets (ElevenLabs audio, Figma exports, Manrope and Inter): no CapCut library audio, stickers, templates or fonts. Exports: organic 9:16 (with the tradie line), a 4:5 FB-feed crop, paid cold variants H1/H2/H4 and retargeting H5 (only the first 2.5s changes; no tradie line on the paid end card).

Skill step-7 checks: the hook lands in under 3s with sound off; the QSME brand is on screen within 0.5s of the swipe; the product is the payoff, not an ad read; still funny on the third watch. Every claim matches research/2026-10-02-qsme-platform-truth.md and the pricing sheet ('Free to join', 'No listing fee on tenders', 'Your own crew is always free', one job sent to the trades you choose, every bidder prices the same lines cut from the SOQ) and there is no bare 'Free', no 'verified', no 'line by line' and no comparison claim. No Meta branding or trade dress; all names fictional; the demo data is off public listings; the AI label is set if the VO is ElevenLabs.

Post on IG, FB and TikTok with cover.png. Link in bio goes straight to the signup or create-project page with utm_source=instagram/facebook/tiktok&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=which-dave. After 3-7 days, record average watch time, shares plus saves per 1,000 views, and comment themes. Go-to-paid rule: average watch time of 15s or more AND shares plus saves of 10 or more per 1,000 views on any one platform.

production_workflow.what: Confirm the Meta Pixel plus Conversions API, and the TikTok Pixel, fire on signup or 'Create a project' (CompleteRegistration or a custom ProjectCreated event), with test events verified. Paid links go to the signup or create-project page, not the homepage, with utm_source=meta/tiktok&utm_medium=paid_social&utm_campaign=which-dave&utm_content=h1/h2/h4/h5. The success-fee line must be visible on the landing page.

production_workflow.step: 12. Paid hook test (only after the user approves a budget)
production_workflow.tool: Meta Ads Manager + TikTok Ads Manager
production_workflow.what: Boost the organic H1 post with Meta 'Use existing post' or TikTok Spark Ads so real comments carry over. H2 and H4 run as new ads, or post them organically first if their comments should carry too. Cold ad set: H1 vs H2 vs H4 with equal budgets of about NZ$15-25/day each for 5-7 days. H5 runs alone in a site-visitor or engager retargeting ad set. Meta primary text: 'Asked the community page for a builder. 212 comments, six Daves, still no builder. Put the actual job on QSME: send one job to the trades you choose, and every one prices the same lines. Free to join.' Headline: 'Know which Dave.' Description: 'Free to join. No listing fee on tenders. Demo data and app recreations shown.' Button: Sign up. TikTok ad text: '212 comments. Six Daves. No builder. Put the actual job on QSME. Free to join.' Starting benchmarks (revise after the first test): hook rate (3s plays / impressions) of 25% or more, hold (ThruPlay / 3s plays) of 30% or more, link CTR of 1% or more. Kill any variant under a 15% hook rate after ~3,000 impressions, then judge the survivors on CPA.
production_workflow.output: learnings.md rows (hook rate, hold, CTR, CPA per variant) + the winning hook

integrity_notes: No real Facebook or Meta branding or trade dress: generic group UI in neutral colours (not FB blue), no 'f', no Meta reaction icons. SFX are generic pings, not the iOS tri-tone or the Messenger pop. On-image copy says 'local group', the VO says 'community page', and nothing says 'Facebook'.

All names are fictional and initials-only (Mel R., Kerry P., Dave K., etc.). Avatars are initials, not AI faces. The group name is now 'Hillcrest Locals (Unofficial)'; search it before locking and record the check in the brief. No business-sounding names like 'Dave Builds'.

Humor punches at the process (hearsay, vague threads, nobody able to check anything), never at tradies or owners. Mel's late line is now '...can anyone actually come and quote?' (2026-10-02, replacing '...is anyone here licensed?'). The 'actually' is aimed at the thread, where everyone names a Dave and nobody offers a quote; it is not a no-show gag about tradies, and Kerry's 'Dave can.' keeps Dave likeable. There are no no-show or dodgy-tradie gags, and Dave is likeable and as lost as everyone else. The half-typed 'Which D|' draft is cut, so Mel stays the straight man.

'212 comments', 'Dave count: 6 (ish)', 'six Daves' and the comment numbers are jokes inside the skit, not claims. There are no customer counts, ratings, reviews, 'X tradies on QSME', speed or savings claims anywhere.

Pricing: never a bare 'Free'. Only the site's own wording is used: 'Free to join' and 'No listing fee' (checked against qsme.co.nz/pricing on 2026-10-02, which also says 'Your first project, free' and a 1% success fee each side, capped at $2,000, invoiced only when a public-marketplace job completes). The ad shows the public-tender flow, so paid ads must show the success-fee line on the landing page. Optional ad description: 'Free to join. No listing fee. Success fee only on completed public-tender jobs.'

No licence or verification claim (fact-check 2026-10-02): licence verification is merged but not confirmed live, and 1 of 22 directory profiles is verified, so 'licence-verified' / 'verified tradies' is on the red list even though the homepage says it. Since 2026-10-02 the licence setup is gone from every format ('Must be licensed' → 'Keen for a few quotes.', '...is anyone here licensed?' → '...can anyone actually come and quote?', 'Dave is.' → 'Dave can.'), so the thread no longer sets up a licensing promise QSME can't keep yet. The payoff is 'Dave count: 1 ✓ — the one you invited', never 'QSME checks Dave's licence'. Don't add a licence line until the owner confirms verification is live.

No 'line by line' (fact-check 2026-10-02): Compare bids is a table of totals per bidder (Excl. GST | GST | Incl. GST, 'Lowest' tag) and each bid opens to its own lines. The side-by-side line matrix is branch-only. 'Same job / same lines for every bidder' is true because the tender is cut from the job's lines. Also avoid 'apples with apples' (the truth sheet says it overstates the screen).

Features claimed (2026-10-02 cut) are limited to: put the actual job on QSME (a project), send one job (a tender cut from the SOQ, private or public) to the trades you choose (invitations from your own contacts), every bidder prices the same lines, free to join, no listing fee on tenders, your own crew is always free (pricing sheet: 'Your own tradies are always free'). The reel no longer shows or claims the Compare bids table; 'every quote in one table, GST shown both ways' stays true but is kept for the H5 variant only. The CCC and document trail is deliberately left out of this one-joke video and saved for the ccc-hunt idea.

Product shots (2026-10-02 cut): one REAL QSME iPhone app capture (seeded demo account, address header covered) and muted, cropped frames from QSME's own narrated walkthrough recreations (mock data), each recreation labelled 'Recreation of the app · mock data' and the still 'QSME iPhone app · demo data'. Crops leave out the 'Quick Jobs' sidebar item (a removed feature), the comparison and publish steps, 'Who can bid / Target trades', contact emails and phone numbers, the 'CRM notes' field and the walkthrough's own captions. Any later owner recording (H5 only) must be on a staging environment or a hidden test org that is excluded from public search and the live projects map, and deleted after filming. Don't mock up a verification badge or a comparison table that differs from the real product. Dave K. is a demo bidder, or a real tradie who has given written consent. The paid ad description includes 'Demo data shown'.
Mel is a skit character, not a testimonial. Her product lines describe what QSME does, not results she 'got' ('Know which Dave' is on-screen text, not 'QSME found me a builder in 2 days').

AI voice disclosure: if Mel's VO comes from ElevenLabs, turn on TikTok's 'AI-generated content' setting and Meta's AI label when posting organically, and add this to the step-9 checklist. Prefer the founder's phone voice memo, which needs no label. There are no AI people anywhere. AI video is only a fallback, and only with disclosure.

No social-proof beat: there is no real proof yet, so the 'proof' role is left out on purpose. For paid, boosting the organic post (Spark Ads or 'Use existing post') carries over its genuine comments. Never seed or write comments ourselves.

Music and assets: one commercially licensed music bed in the master for every version. No trending copyrighted tracks, no in-app music, and no CapCut library audio, stickers, templates or fonts in branded exports. Prompts and licence receipts are saved in projects/<slug>/outputs/licences/.
open_questions: How is QSME said out loud: 'Q-S-M-E' or 'kiss-me'? Your message reads like it was dictated as 'kiss me'. The VO says the brand twice ('...on QSME'), so this blocks the voice recording and the ElevenLabs pronunciation alias.

(Resolved 2026-10-02: the licence setup is swapped for the quote setup everywhere, so nothing implies QSME checks licences.) Licence verification: the fact-check (2026-10-02) found it merged but not confirmed live (1 of 22 profiles verified, LBP lookup only if the MBIE key is set). Until you confirm it's live, the video makes no licence claim. Do you want to soften Mel's 'Must be licensed' setup so viewers don't infer QSME checks licences, or keep it as a pure skit line? (Current call: keep it; the payoff only claims you know which Dave quoted.)

Pricing wording: the live /pricing page says 'Your first project, free' plus a 1% success fee each side (capped at $2,000) on completed public-tender jobs. Is a second project charged? Confirm the exact fee line to show on the paid landing page and in the ad description.

(Only for the optional H5 variant now; the main cut needs no owner recording.) Is there a hidden demo org excluded from public search and the live projects map, where you can create 'Bathroom + deck, Hillcrest', send the tender and add a demo bid from 'Dave K.' to screen-record (we never log in)? Or is there a real QSME builder (bonus if he's really a Dave) who'd consent to appear?

Organic only to start, or is there a paid budget? The suggested cold test is about NZ$15-25/day per variant x 3 variants x 5-7 days, roughly NZ$225-525, plus a small H5 retargeting set. Are the QSME IG and TikTok accounts business accounts? Are the Meta Pixel plus CAPI and the TikTok Pixel installed on signup / 'Create a project'?

Voice: will you or a real Kiwi owner record the ~40-word VO on a phone (better for trust, no AI label), or should we use ElevenLabs? Female or male? Does your ElevenLabs plan permit commercial use of VO, SFX and music?
Is Hamilton/Hillcrest the right place to set it, or should it be where QSME has the most projects (e.g. Auckland, Christchurch)?
Do you want a tradie-side cut as well? Same thread, but the ending is for Dave: 'Stop quoting off a comment. Join as a tradie.' QSME is two-sided, so it would reach both audiences.
Brand assets for Figma: logo files and exact colour values. Fonts are noted as Manrope 800 and Inter in ventures/qsme-nz.md; confirm they're current.
Does QSME NZ post on LinkedIn for small developers? If not, the LinkedIn carousel is dropped from this package.
Do you want the same package for qsme.build next ('Six quotes, six formats', LinkedIn-first, neutral international English, 'Book a 30-minute demo')?
changelog: Peak split into two beats with no VO (Humor must-fix): 9.0-11.0 hard stop on Dave K. with 2.0s of total silence and the tally going to '?'; 11.0-13.5 Mel's question, then 'Dave is.' 0.6s later, then a silent hold, with the swipe as Mel's reaction. 'Cheers, Dave.' is deleted from the script, the captions and the voice-test plan. Conflict: the Platform critique's retimed sheet kept 'Cheers, Dave.'. I kept its timing and legibility fixes but not that line, because it fills the silence that sells the laugh and thanks the wrong person.

Product section tightened to one idea (Humor must-fix): CCC is cut from the reel, carousel and caption and saved for the ccc-hunt idea. The product is now two moments (create a project, then quotes arriving line by line), followed by a VO-free Dave K. payoff where the single ding is the punchline and the tally redraws to 'Dave count: 1' with a tick. 'Finally.' is dropped. 'Know which Dave' now lands ~10s after the peak instead of ~13s. Conflict: the Platform critique's carousel fix kept the CCC line; the must-fix wins.

Spoken CTA reconciled across both must-fixes: the VO is now 'Put the job on QSME. Free to join.', with no spoken URL, no bare 'Free', and no spoken brand straight after a line ending in 'Dave' (21.0-25.5 is VO-free). On screen, everywhere: 'Free to join. No listing fee. qsme.co.nz'. Every 'Create a project. Free.' is removed. I checked the wording against live qsme.co.nz/pricing and the homepage on 2026-10-02: 'no listing fee', 'Your first project, free', a 1% success fee each side capped at $2,000 on completion, and 'Licence-verified contractors, trades and consultants'. The fee line is now required on the paid landing page and offered for the ad description.

The fixed body now explains itself for every hook (Platform must-fix + Humor should-fix): at 2.5-3.5 Mel's post card fills the screen with 'Must be licensed' underlined in red, then shrinks into a pinned header (y 300-400) for the whole problem section. That sets up 'Dave is.' in H1, H2, H4 and H5 alike.

Legibility (Platform must-fix): only the 0-2.5s hook is phone-in-hand. From 2.5s it's a full-frame 1080x1920 screen recording with text at least 44px. Every Dave comment is held at least 0.9s, and the peak gets 2.0s.

Brand clarity (Platform must-fix): on-screen text at the swipe is now 'Or. Post the actual job on QSME.' and the QSME wordmark must be visible in the app header within 0.5s. The VO says the same words, so the on-screen text doubles as the caption.

Safe zones (Platform must-fix): all text and logos sit inside x 65-1015, y 300-1250. The Dave count moved from top-right to upper-left. Deviation: it's at y 420-500, not the suggested y 320-420, because the new pinned post header now occupies y 300-400. The end-card CTA is at y 1000-1200 with the logo above, and both overlays are checked in CapCut.

Escalation re-paced (Humor should-fix + Platform must-fix): scroll, stop, scroll. Stop 1.2s on 'Deck Dave or Roof Dave?' and 1.4s on 'Big Dave did ours. Not Little Dave.', and the three 'Following' lines blur past in 0.6s (between the reviewers' 0.5s and 0.8s). The tally ticks land on the stops.

VO trimmed (Humor should-fix): no VO from 2.5 to 5.5. 'Got a Dave. Then two more.' is not reinstated (the Platform sheet had it) because the comments plus the tally already carry it. '[sighs] Following. Following.' is deleted. Only the flat roll call 'Deck Dave. Roof Dave. Big Dave. Little Dave.' remains, timed to the stops. The VO total is now ~40 words, so step 2 says ~40 (the Platform note said ~60, but that was counted before these cuts).

The tally no longer appears in the hook (Humor should-fix). It first scribbles in as 'Dave count: 1' when Kerry's comment lands, which is a small reveal of its own. The H1 text layer is now just '212 comments. Still no builder.'
Sam's line changed to 'Hillcrest Dave or the other Hillcrest Dave?' (Humor should-fix) in the reel, static and carousel, so the peak is the first time anyone asks 'Which Dave'.

The half-typed 'Which D|' reply box is cut from carousel slide 5 (Humor should-fix), so 'Dave is.' stands alone. Conflict: the Platform critique listed it as a keep. I sided with Humor because it's a third joke on the slide meant for 'Dave is.', and if it's Mel's draft it pulls the straight man into the mess.

'actually' is removed from Mel's line in every format (Humor should-fix): '...is anyone here licensed?' everywhere. The Platform sheet used 'actually', but it edges toward a dodgy-tradie hint, which is off-limits for this venture.

Payoff wording: 'Verified trades' became 'Licence-verified trades' in the on-screen bullet, VO, caption, static subline and carousel (Platform should-fix; it's the site's own wording, used organically now and substantiated before paid). 'Apples to apples' became 'Apples with apples' in the VO (Humor fix; the natural Kiwi phrasing).
Hook VO is now 'Asked the community page for a builder.' (Humor nice). The on-screen copy and H4 keep 'local group'.

Caption rewritten (Humor should-fix): it opens 'Asked for a builder. Got Dave. Several of him.' and the engagement line is 'Got a good Dave? Tag him.' It ends with the product line and 'qsme.co.nz (link in bio)' (Platform nice). Conflict: the Platform critique wanted to keep 'How many Daves did your thread get?' as the last line. I replaced it because the tag prompt still invites comments, adds reach through tagging, and turns the joke into a shout-out for good tradies on a two-sided marketplace.
Captions are only burned in for VO lines that aren't already on screen (Platform should-fix). The comments are the captions during the escalation.

Music: one commercially licensed bed now goes into the CapCut master for every version, organic and paid, and in-app music is never added (Platform must-fix). It enters at 13.5s. Licence receipts go to outputs/licences/. Generic-ping SFX prompt added (Platform nice).

Voice direction: 'Waikato-ish' became 'general everyday New Zealand accent', and 'not Australian, not British' is added to the Voice Design prompt. Voices are shortlisted on the roll call and the CTA line, rejecting any where 'deck' or 'little' sounds Aussie (Humor should-fix). The default model is now Multilingual v2, since no audio tags remain.

New integrity notes: AI voice disclosure on TikTok and Meta if the VO is ElevenLabs, and the founder memo is preferred (Platform should-fix). Demo Dave K. only on a staging or hidden org excluded from public search and the map, deleted after filming, with 'Demo data shown' in the paid description (Platform should-fix). CapCut library assets are banned from branded exports (Platform should-fix).

Paid plan rebuilt (Platform must-fix + should-fixes): a conversion-tracking step before any spend (Meta Pixel + CAPI, TikTok Pixel, a ProjectCreated or CompleteRegistration event, per-variant UTMs, a direct signup link). A cold ad set of H1 vs H2 vs H4 (rebuilt text-only, no person) at about NZ$15-25/day each for 5-7 days, with H5 alone in retargeting. Numeric go-to-paid, benchmark and kill thresholds. Paid end card without the tradie line. Meta and TikTok ad-copy fields. Spark Ads or 'Use existing post' so genuine comments carry over. Every paid step is gated on the user's explicit budget yes.

H4 rebuilt as text-only over the thread with VO 'You've met Dave. Several of him.' (Platform should-fix). 'Several of him' also moves into the caption (Humor should-fix). H5's VO is now 'Spoiler: it's this Dave. The group took 212 comments to not find him.' (Platform nice), and its payoff repeat is noted as an intentional bookend for retargeting.

Carousel cut from 8 to 7 slides (Platform should-fix): slides 2 and 3 merged into 'Comments 1 and 2' with a top strip restating the question, so it works as an entry point. The product slide uses ONE large real comparison screenshot and three short lines, with Humor's 'Post the job once.' line replacing the CCC line. The final slide reads 'Know which Dave. Free to join. No listing fee. qsme.co.nz'. Also relabelled the Mel and Kerry slide 'Comments 211 and 212', since it holds two comments.

Static thinned (Platform should-fix): 7 comments (Jase dropped here; his line stays in the reel and carousel). Comment text is at least 34px. The screenshot crop is removed from the end band, which is now text only ('Know which Dave.' in Manrope 800, the subline, 'Free to join. No listing fee. qsme.co.nz', small logo). A light red underline under 'Must be licensed' is added so the static carries the same setup as the reel.

Group name changed to 'Hillcrest Locals (Unofficial)', with a search check recorded in the brief (Platform nice). Counter animation reduced to three states, 197, 205 and 212 (Platform nice). cover.png specified for IG and TikTok (Platform nice). LinkedIn dropped by default, kept only as a 1080x1350 PDF with at most 3 hashtags if the user confirms (Platform nice).
Not applied yet: Humor's 'Are any of these Daves LBP?' line. It depends on QSME confirming that its verification covers LBP, so it's now part of the licences open question.

Kept unchanged, as both reviewers asked: the premise and core joke, H1 as the chosen hook, the thread lines in NZ English, Dave's comment alone at the peak, 'Dave is.', the Dave-count running gag ending in a tick, ping rhythm into silence into a single ding, 'Or. Post the actual job.' and 'Know which Dave.', the marked-up-screenshot static, generic non-Meta UI, no invented proof, real demo screens only, real hands and no AI people, and the cheap Figma, iPhone, ElevenLabs and CapCut path.

2026-10-02 fact-check fix: removed 'Licence-verified trades/tradies' (licence verification not confirmed live; 1 of 22 profiles verified) and 'compared line by line' / 'apples with apples' (Compare bids is a totals table excl./incl. GST with a 'Lowest' tag; each bid opens to its own lines; the line matrix is branch-only). New copy: 'Tradies quote on the same job' / 'Every quote in one table, GST shown both ways' / 'Know which Dave.' (Dave K.'s bid opens to its own lines, no badge). Static subline: 'Tradies quote on the same job. Every quote in one table.' Earlier changelog entries that mention the old wording are kept as history and are superseded by this one.
